| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. body:

Please read the message below from our sponsor.
* * *
| | | [](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbqxrt&__onlt=h)
---
| | Friend,
---
| | Charlie would have wanted you to have this.

Before his September 10th assassination, Charlie had just put the finishing touches on a very important book. His final book.

The topic is one that Charlie found to be crucial for every human to understand and practice.

This isn’t a book about public policy or political discourse, nor is it simply about passing on values of patriotism to young Americans.

**Instead, this book is about something far deeper and more personal — the importance of honoring the Sabbath and resting in God’s grace.**

Despite his hectic schedule and full life, Charlie was committed to setting aside an entire day each week to rest, to pray, and to give undivided attention to God, Erika, and his children.

By honoring the Sabbath, Charlie lived out a powerful message: _**“God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold.”**_

His book, _**Stop, in the Name of God**_ is the fruit of that conviction.
---
[](https://trk.thedcbugle.com/?&eih=kzm8nstj6prmj7bhz7sjvvnysq73bagh&__stmp=tbqxrt&__onlt=h)
---
When you read it, you will hear Charlie’s voice inviting you to reclaim something our fast-paced culture has essentially erased: a time for rest, a time devoted to God, and time with family.

Charlie’s hope was for each of us to rediscover the Sabbath as he did: not as a burden to bear, but as a gift to receive...

A sacred routine meant to draw us nearer to God, to steady our hearts with His peace, and renew our strength for the battles to which He calls us.

I believe you will find this book inspiring.

Charlie wanted everyone to have this book because its message meant so much in his own life.

Fellow Patriot,

My very good friend, Chip Roy, is running for Texas Attorney General.

I've known Chip for a long time, and I can tell you with 100% certainty that there has been no fiercer fighter for the America First agenda than Chip.

No one - _and I really mean it_ - has fought harder to help President Trump scrap the policies of the Biden years and put our country on a path toward prosperity.

**In Congress, Chip has been a relentless voice for the conservative principles Texans believe in.**

He's fought to stop the cartels that are flooding our communities with drugs and crime.

He's the leading voice in Congress fighting to protect the integrity of our elections and end voter fraud.

And most importantly, he's working with President Trump to secure the border.

| | Dear Peter,
---
Spring is a great season for listening to podcasts. Maybe you like to indulge while hiking through wildflower-carpeted hills. Perhaps your podcast playlist is a cherished companion on a spring road trip. Or you just like to pull on headphones and listen while tackling spring cleaning.
---
Wherever you enjoy your podcasts, here’s your next great binge-listen: All eight episodes of Season 5 of Save the Redwoods League’s podcast, **_[I’ll Go If You Go](https://click.everyaction.com/k/127132203/607036968/-849153485?utm_campaign=igiyg&utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-mar&utm_content=season-5&sourceid=1168533&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM3ZTk5YTA1LTc4MWQtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a2qpeda4OfNtK53edJhSxhd6Kc-E6aU-gNLeq-W_rm4=&emci=8bc7f37d-b21c-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=c7e99a05-781d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=1504551)_** , are now available.
---
---

---
Episode 6 spotlights the often invisible crews that build and repair beloved trails.
---
Guided by host Monica Carcamo-Binetti, you’ll hear from the founder of City Gurlz Hike about the importance of creating belonging in nature; learn how to find the wild in our own backyards with state park staff; and discover how time spent in the redwoods benefits your whole self, right down to the cellular level. We created _I'll Go If You Go_ to build togetherness and connection in the outdoors by handing the mic to a diverse chorus of voices shaping California’s wild places. And it's getting noticed—we’re proud to say _I’ll Go If You Go_ was recently recognized as one of the **[15 Best California Outdoor Podcasts](https://click.everyaction.com/k/127132204/607036969/-1297327802?utm_campaign=igiyg&utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-mar&utm_content=season-5&sourceid=1168533&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM3ZTk5YTA1LTc4MWQtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a2qpeda4OfNtK53edJhSxhd6Kc-E6aU-gNLeq-W_rm4=&emci=8bc7f37d-b21c-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=c7e99a05-781d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=1504551)****[ ](https://click.everyaction.com/k/127132205/607036970/-1297327802?utm_campaign=igiyg&utm_medium=email&utm_source=ea-mar&utm_content=season-5&sourceid=1168533&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9TVFJXTC9TVFJXTC8xLzg5NTc0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogImM3ZTk5YTA1LTc4MWQtZjExMS05YTQ4LTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=a2qpeda4OfNtK53edJhSxhd6Kc-E6aU-gNLeq-W_rm4=&emci=8bc7f37d-b21c-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=c7e99a05-781d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=1504551)** by Feedspot. The most recent season is a great place to jump right in and immerse yourself. Just grab your headphones and press play.
---
| | Happy listening,

clean_body: Ready to binge: All 8 episodes of our I’ll Go If You Go podcast| | | | | | | | | Dear Peter, Spring is a great season for listening to podcasts. Maybe you like to indulge while hiking through wildflower-carpeted hills. Perhaps your podcast playlist is a cherished companion on a spring road trip. Or you just like to pull on headphones and listen while tackling spring cleaning. Wherever you enjoy your podcasts, here’s your next great binge-listen: All eight episodes of Season 5 of Save the Redwoods League’s podcast, , are now available. Episode 6 spotlights the often invisible crews that build and repair beloved trails. Guided by host Monica Carcamo-Binetti, you’ll hear from the founder of City Gurlz Hike about the importance of creating belonging in nature; learn how to find the wild in our own backyards with state park staff; and discover how time spent in the redwoods benefits your whole self, right down to the cellular level. We created I'll Go If You Go to build togetherness and connection in the outdoors by handing the mic to a diverse chorus of voices shaping California’s wild places. And it's getting noticed—we’re proud to say I’ll Go If You Go was recently recognized as one of the by Feedspot. The most recent season is a great place to jump right in and immerse yourself. Just grab your headphones and press play. | | Happy listening, Save the Redwoods League Photos from top: Lisa Erdberg; courtesy of Monica Carcamo-Binetti | | Save the Redwoods League 220 Montgomery Street, Suite 350 San Francisco, CA 94104 United States CONNECT WITH US | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|--- |

All across Pennsylvania, folks are fired up not only to push back against the division and extremism coming from DC — but to keep building on the progress our Commonwealth has made over the last three years. To bring down costs and put money back into Pennsylvanians’ pockets. To make our public schools even stronger. To create more opportunity and advance real freedom here in Pennsylvania. That’s the future I’m fighting for every single day. A future where we treat each other with respect, defend our fundamental freedoms, and focus on progress and solutions instead of division and distraction. **But Derek, I’m not naive.** In Pennsylvania and all across the country, there are those who _don’t_ believe in the same freedoms we do. Tell Chief Justice Roberts to do the right thing
| **Friend, the Supreme Court may be about to greenlight MAGA’s wildest voter suppression fantasies.** [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104517?t=6&akid=23225%2E878179%2Eo7QFu1) [Friend: Add your name now to our viral letter DEMANDING Chief Justice Roberts and the Supreme Court SAVE The Voting Rights Act! »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104517?t=7&akid=23225%2E878179%2Eo7QFu1) | [**RUSH $3 TO ADD YOUR NAME »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104517?t=8&akid=23225%2E878179%2Eo7QFu1)

TO: Chief Justice John Roberts
FROM: A Proud Democrat
SUBJECT: Protect the Voting Rights Act
_Chief Justice John Roberts,_

I know Donald Trump and Mike Johnson are pressuring you to destroy The Voting Rights Act.

**But at a time when our democracy is already under unprecedented threat,_this would be a disaster_ for the American public.**

Now is the time to restore faith in our democratic system and stand up to those who wish to take complete power for themselves – not make it more vulnerable.

I know Trump sees the end of the Voting Rights Act as another path to holding onto his majorities despite his crashing popularity. **It’s critical you stand against this.**

[That’s why I’m adding my signature and donating $3 to the Voter Protection Project to make clear my TOTAL opposition to destroying the Voting Rights Act »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104517?t=9&akid=23225%2E878179%2Eo7QFu1) | [**RUSH $3 TO ADD YOUR NAME »**](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/104517?t=10&akid=23225%2E878179%2Eo7QFu1)

**X A Proud Democrat**

**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends,
Heidi fills in for today's Mountain Minute podcast: Listen [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Here is a summary of today's top stories:
🏛️ **Under the Golden Dome...** A Democratic lawmaker has [shelved a proposal to decriminalize prostitution](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after acknowledging it lacked the votes to pass the Senate Judiciary Committee. Meanwhile, [concealed handgun permits remain widely sought](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite new restrictions, with more than 19% of Colorado adults estimated to hold a permit. Separately, critics warn that [“blight” designations used in redevelopment plans](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) can unlock tax subsidies and eminent domain powers for projects such as a potential new Broncos stadium site.

🏔️ **Here in Colorado...** Secretary of State Jena Griswold has [asked DHS to confirm ICE agents will not be stationed at polling places](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) in 2026. Xcel Energy warned delays in new generation and damage to Comanche Unit 3 could create a near-term power shortfall, proposing to [keep several coal units running through 2030](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Separately, a Colorado Department of Agriculture manager who challenged DEI-related training listed in a federally tied pest survey report is [facing possible discipline after raising concerns](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) about how the program was being reported.
🇺🇸**On the National Stage...** Federal investigators have subpoenaed voting records from Arizona’s Maricopa County as part of a [probe into suspected election irregularities](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), while a federal affidavit alleges a [deported noncitizen voted in five presidential elections](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Meanwhile, critics warn a provision in the [bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) could discourage new rental housing construction, and commentary is raising concerns about [inconsistent media framing](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) of foreign authoritarian leaders versus domestic conservatives.

This is your Mountain Minute for Wednesday, March 11, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado agriculture manager faces discipline after dispute over federal grant report and DEI training](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
A Colorado Department of Agriculture manager who challenged training language in a federally tied pest survey report now faces possible discipline after an internal investigation concluded he “more likely than not” misrepresented the document.
The dispute follows [earlier RMV reporting](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that raised questions about DEI-related training references appearing in a report tied to a USDA cooperative agreement.
The issue grew out of a 2025 CAPS Infrastructure Accomplishment Report tied to a USDA cooperative agreement. In one section, the document lists training entries including “Equity and Diversity” and “Inclusive Leadership.”
CDA says Rich Guggenheim shared a screenshot of what it describes as a draft report and wrongly portrayed it as evidence that the department was using federal funds for DEI programs. Guggenheim says the document was part of the reporting process and that he raised concerns internally before the conflict escalated.

**[Colorado Democrat Shelves Prostitution Decriminalization Effort Amid Growing Criticism](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [THE DAILY SIGNAL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Colorado Democrat shelves prostitution decriminalization bill:** State Sen. Nick Hinrichsen announced he will delay SB26-097—effectively killing the measure after acknowledging it lacked support to pass the Senate Judiciary Committee.
* **Sponsor cites concerns about hostile hearing:** Hinrichsen said supporters worried about a contentious committee hearing where “sex workers” might face law enforcement, religious leaders, and other critics, and concluded the effort was unlikely to succeed.
* **Opponents lined up heavily against proposal:** Colorado Republicans noted that 42 people had signed up to testify against the bill and only one in favor, arguing lawmakers should hear from community voices concerned about public safety and trafficking risks.

**[Griswold Joins Other States Asking DHS To Confirm ICE Will Stay Away From Polling Locations](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [DENVER GAZETTE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
* **Colorado joins multi-state request on ICE at polling places:** Secretary of State Jena Griswold announced Colorado has formally asked the Department of Homeland Security for written confirmation that ICE agents will not be stationed at polling locations during the 2026 election cycle.
* **Request comes despite prior DHS statement:** The letter follows comments from former DHS Secretary Kristi Noem saying there were no plans to place ICE officers at polling sites.
* **Part of coordinated effort with other blue states:** Colorado joined eight states—including Oregon, Washington, and Illinois—in asking the incoming DHS leadership to confirm ICE will have no presence at polling locations ahead of the June primary and November general elections.

# [Defeating Fascists Isn't Enough. We Need to Prosecute Them.](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=190623725&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwNjIzNzI1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzMyNTU4MTQsImV4cCI6MTc3NTg0NzgxNCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.YIUa64670BQELI3WMNjzT7TbBu6t3pDrGbOUXJKgmjI)
### Holding the powerful accountable for their crimes is the only way out of this mess.
| | [Aaron Regunberg](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)
---
| Mar 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/@aaronregunberg)

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=190623725&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwNjIzNzI1LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc3MzI1NTgxNCwiZXhwIjoxNzc1ODQ3ODE0LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItNDk4MTE3MCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.slEsqYgMxgjIZpFJ697uBhiX4RZ9y6fE2QMeHkr-I20&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

As we stumble through the smoking ruins of our democracy and gaze across the grotesqueries that stalk its burnt-out rubble--the incalculable corruption, the horrific wars of aggression, the point-blank execution of American civilians by federal goon squads--it's only natural to search for the decision points that set us on this course. If I had to identify a single figure whose choices led us here, I'd be hard pressed to find a greater culprit than former Attorney General Merrick Garland.
Given everything that has happened since Donald Trump returned to power last January, you could hardly be blamed if you were unaware that Garland--who Barack Obama unsuccessfully nominated to replace Antonin Scalia on the Supreme Court and who served as Joe Biden's attorney general--got a new job. It's an old job, really: He returned to the corporate law firm Arnold & Porter, where he had previously been a partner, to work on [focus areas](https://substack.com/redirect/0be9c80d-5cee-40e3-8df4-f5ecbeee73cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) including white collar defense.
Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9hYXJvbnJlZ3VuYmVyZy5zdWJzdGFjay5jb20vYWNjb3VudCIsInAiOjE5MDYyMzcyNSwicyI6NDk4MTE3MCwiZiI6dHJ1ZSwidSI6OTA1MDExOTIsImlhdCI6MTc3MzI1NTgxNCwiZXhwIjoyMDg4ODMxODE0LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMCIsInN1YiI6ImxpbmstcmVkaXJlY3QifQ.OaA6b6H2-kMnkpj2liRvTYn78VTEjJzM14zg4JxTyWQ?)
White collar defense, which often involves helping the rich and powerful escape accountability, is also the best way to describe Garland's tenure as attorney general, at least where it matters. While Garland's DOJ immediately began to prosecute the lowest-level participants in Trump's crimes against democracy--the foot soldiers of Jan. 6--Garland steadfastly refused to take on the architect of that insurrection, [waiting almost three years](https://substack.com/redirect/5a53aa65-a523-4b04-8cbb-278cb0a9f6bb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to bring federal charges against Trump himself. Indeed, Garland only took action after Congress's Jan. 6 committee [essentially forced](https://substack.com/redirect/729f4d01-46f9-4438-ba2c-38c8f41b00db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) him to launch the prosecutorial effort he'd spent years resisting. By that time, it was--in the most predictable way imaginable--already too late. Trump was running for reelection, meaning he could cast his prosecution as political persecution. He would be reelected before the cases against him had any chance to be concluded. Where accountability mattered, Garland failed spectacularly.
This, and the resulting dystopian reality we are living through today, were not necessary or foregone conclusions. Another path was eminently possible, as a veritable pileup of international counterexamples demonstrates. Just this February, South Korea's former president Yoon Suk Yeol was [jailed for life](https://substack.com/redirect/f0a0408a-acfd-4546-8087-66f1c92bd71a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for his imposition of martial law in December 2024. Last November, a Peruvian court [handed down](https://substack.com/redirect/a09c8053-8e64-4086-b463-48f793cfe901?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an 11-year sentence to former president Pedro Castillo for his attempt to dissolve Peru's Congress in December 2022. And last September, Brazil's highest court [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/52fbf09d-bc81-4892-b354-54dc2cdbc59f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) former president Jair Bolsonaro to 27 years in prison for his efforts to overturn that country's 2022 election results.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/dc660b59-33be-46a8-955f-10ae34a0115a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Brazilian comparison is particularly instructive, because of the beat-for-beat similarities between Bolsonaro and Trump. Both are right-wing populists who falsely insisted they had won an election they had lost. Both used tactics of denial and conspiracy to inspire violent attacks against their respective capitols with the goal of blocking a democratic transition of power. But the paths of these authoritarian despots diverged sharply following their attempted coups. One is currently in prison. The other is back in control of the most powerful nation on Earth, waging an all-out assault on our Constitution that frankly makes the crimes of his first term look like child's play.
Given this tragic sequence of events, it is not, I think, too soon for those of us opposed to Trump's corrupt and cruel reign of terror--and in particular for our ostensible opposition party, whose leaders failed so utterly in their previous attempt to bring Trump to justice--to begin thinking seriously about what accountability for the crimes of this regime will look like if (and needless to say, it is a big if) Democrats are able to take back Congress and the presidency. Clearly, the Garland approach failed. What should replace it?
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/88d7f50b-8282-49e7-8811-a9899617f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The only appropriate answer is the zealous pursuit of justice at every level of this criminal enterprise of an administration. The next Democratic administration should extend the Garland approach to January 6--a focus on the criminal foot soldiers of the Trump regime--to a host of other areas, most notably immigration enforcement, foreign policy, and corruption. But it shouldn't stop there, as the response to January 6 did. It must go further.
Justice not only for the ICE and CBP thugs who murdered Americans in the streets, but also for the senior advisors and cabinet secretaries who sent those thugs on their campaigns of stochastic terrorism. Justice for the goons who will, it seems [increasingly likely](https://substack.com/redirect/56e9ac7e-630e-4bf2-8b72-a14a49e92a37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), seek to rig our upcoming elections, and the higher-level apparatchiks devising those antidemocratic schemes. Justice not just for the officials who executed double-tap strikes against civilians and bombed elementary schools and committed other startlingly [barbaric war crimes](https://substack.com/redirect/a26529a7-4a5f-4cde-8c1c-9d06b5566527?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but more importantly, for the leaders who criminally launched such brazenly illegal military actions and wars. And, of course, justice for everyone inside and outside of this administration engaging in the most incomprehensibly [flagrant looting](https://substack.com/redirect/e6ab4ae6-a1d0-4218-b5e6-55073efcabd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of America's public resources in our history.
Admittedly, all of this is a tall order. Pursuing accountability with such breadth and depth would require a serious commitment of resources, attention, and political capital. But it's a necessary, not an optional, step towards rebuilding our democracy, which--even in this ideal future in which Democrats have overcome Trump's efforts to dismantle free elections to win back temporary control of the government--will be overwhelmingly fragile for a long time to come. As the Allies understood when devising their [denazification programs](https://substack.com/redirect/1365108f-7bd1-4f3b-80ad-0997821d9275?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for Germany after World War II, America simply cannot afford to allow the bandits, propagandists, and sadists who've been running this administration to simply slide back into positions of power and privilege from which to plot their next fascist takeover. If Garland's ignominious tenure as attorney general achieved nothing else of value, let it at least have taught us this lesson.
Of course, these prosecutions would be polarizing; in today's political environment, there's little that is not, though much of this administration's conduct that merits prosecution enjoys supermajority levels of reprobation from the public. But a push for accountability, to succeed, will require a demonstration of popular support--in other words, a mandate. And that means it is incumbent on Democrats to make this fight for accountability a key part of their platform, starting now.
This will make many Democratic leaders squeamish. The party's centrist establishment hates to take strong stances on just about anything. And there may be opposition from some on the left, as well. After all, doesn't this "prosecute Trump" fixation risk dragging us back to a pre-2020 resistance liberalism that deprioritized material conditions and obscured the structural problems of oligarchy, of which Trump is really just a symptom?
Well, it could, if done poorly. But it could also buttress a much more powerful populist message, of the kind that Democrats desperately need to embrace if they are going to beat the diminished but still-potent right-wing populism of Trump and his MAGA heirs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/88d7f50b-8282-49e7-8811-a9899617f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The word "populism" is thrown around a lot to describe very different political tendencies, in large part because populist anger can be channeled in polar opposite directions, towards fascism on the one hand or social democracy on the other. But at its core, populism is what you get when a critical mass of a society stops seeing the previous systems of political authority as legitimate. And there is nothing--literally nothing--that creates that perception of illegitimacy more than repeated demonstrations of elite impunity.
This dynamic is the foundation of our current political crisis. Indeed, elite impunity is what created Donald Trump, whose pledges to tear the system down triumphed twice against candidates who responded to his anti-system rhetoric by defending that system. In 2016 and 2024 Trump cast himself as an outsider who was being attacked precisely because he represented a threat to America's political establishment and economic and cultural elite. For many, the alarm with which Trump was greeted only solidified this status. Finally, someone was promising to deliver some much-needed punishment to those who deserved it. In a world where regular people have watched again and again as rich assholes hollowed out their communities and denuded their lives and faced zero consequences for their crimes, Trump's [exhortation](https://substack.com/redirect/bf697b3e-e5d5-4211-8823-405cb849c549?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--"For those who've been wronged and betrayed, I am your retribution"--starts to sound pretty good. At least someone's talking about retribution.
Obviously, that was never the reality of Trumpism, and today Trump's administration stands as the ultimate monument to elite impunity. There are countless examples of how his regime has become a platonic ideal of the corrupt swamp, from the [pardon-for-cash](https://substack.com/redirect/a0be1ce6-4b81-4d33-a8ce-9100d80d7858?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) operation it has been running for wealthy criminals of all stripes, to the DOJ's announcement that it simply won't be [prosecuting corporate crimes](https://substack.com/redirect/02addf6c-3fa1-4d61-ad82-9552cf01369d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) anymore. But the clearest narrative connecting Trump and elite impunity--indeed, the most intuitively understandable indictment of how our institutions have failed to hold elites accountable for their depravity--is the one that's for months been flowing out of the millions of documents that make up the Epstein files.
It's worth noting here that our old friend Merrick Garland sat on the Epstein files for four years without raising a finger to seek justice for Epstein's victims or raise awareness about his accomplices, enablers, and associates--the latter group of which includes Epstein's longtime friend Donald Trump, who sent him a [pornographic birthday](https://substack.com/redirect/25b52d38-eb7a-40e5-b7e6-3747c301db6f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) card referencing a "wonderful secret" that would "never age," and who has been accused of trafficking and sexually assaulting a 13-year-old girl whom the FBI later found credible enough to [interview](https://substack.com/redirect/669f4d2e-9f8d-45a6-9445-d72834975f54?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) four times.
Thanks to horrifying references like these, the Trump administration has become deeply entangled and, in the eyes of many voters, incriminated in the Epstein saga. And that means Democrats have an opportunity to develop a broader message of opposition to elite impunity--one that rightfully combines pledges to hold both Epstein's associates and the Trump administration accountable for their wanton criminality. Because the truth is, these two groups are one and the same. As Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff [aptly put it](https://substack.com/redirect/65ea6117-e41e-4867-9f08-b8f46bbd959d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "We were told that MAGA was for working-class Americans. But this is a government of, by, and for the ultra-rich. It's the wealthiest cabinet ever. This is the Epstein class. They are the elites they pretend to hate."
It's a message Democrats can run--and govern--on. Remember the system you so despised, with its one set of rules for you and me and another for the wealthy and powerful? The system that let Jeffrey Epstein off with a slap on the wrist because he was rich and well-connected? The system that transferred teen sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell to a cushy minimum security prison where she [reportedly](https://substack.com/redirect/72ac8852-753d-4651-b818-61b0b81c9640?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is waited on hand and foot by prison officials and was given a puppy? Well, that's the same system that's been working to protect Epstein's longtime friend Donald Trump and all his sycophantic deputies--like Trump's Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, a documented visitor to Epstein's pedophile island--from being held accountable for their many crimes. And this time it's the Democrats who are promising to burn that god-forsaken system of elite impunity down to the ground.
Of course, it would be madness at this point to trust the Democratic establishment--so long led by the likes of [Bill Clinton](https://substack.com/redirect/baa0130e-e826-4f58-bac9-9445e571fe59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Reid Hoffman](https://substack.com/redirect/98cd3685-a9db-40ab-95d3-158d78b33862?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Larry Summers](https://substack.com/redirect/6daa52da-3f82-422d-bfdd-ec74f858f4c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), each of whom spent years consorting with Epstein--to embrace this message. Thankfully, 2028 offers Democrats an opportunity to wipe the slate clean of their decrepitly complicit establishment.
This is one of the Democrats' greatest advantages right now. As Marjorie Taylor Greene's [expulsion](https://substack.com/redirect/a3ea178b-01ec-4acf-aed7-22cc12c65287?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from GOP politics has demonstrated, taking on Epstein means taking on Trump, and no politician can become the next Republican presidential nominee by running against Trump. But our next Democratic nominee absolutely can--and must--commit to waging a war on the Epstein class, prosecuting its horrors, and rooting out the larger culture of elite impunity that is destroying our country from within. That promise not only gives Democrats a powerful populist message to run on--it also sets them up to demonstrate a real popular mandate, post-election, to bring the perpetrators of this regime's horrific crimes to justice.
This January, Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva held a rally in front of a massive banner reading "Defense of Democracy." He was there to veto legislation that Brazil's opposition-controlled Congress had passed to lower Bolsonaro's sentence from 27 to two years. After describing Bolsonaro's attempted coup as a reminder that "democracy is not an unshakeable achievement," [Lula proclaimed](https://substack.com/redirect/d23d912d-58d6-4ae1-a869-419e2bc262d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "In the name of the future, we do not have the right to forget the past." Unlike Lula, America's last Democratic administration failed to appreciate this essential truth. It is quite possible that this failure will prove lethal to our democracy. But if it's not--if we are so fortunate as to have an opportunity to drive MAGA from power in 2026 and 2028--Democrats cannot be allowed to repeat their past mistakes. We must bring the architects of our current nightmare to justice--not in the name of the past, but in the name of the future.

clean_body: Holding the powerful accountable for their crimes is the only way out of this mess. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Holding the powerful accountable for their crimes is the only way out of this mess. | | | Mar 11 | | | | | | | | | | | | As we stumble through the smoking ruins of our democracy and gaze across the grotesqueries that stalk its burnt-out rubble--the incalculable corruption, the horrific wars of aggression, the point-blank execution of American civilians by federal goon squads--it's only natural to search for the decision points that set us on this course. If I had to identify a single figure whose choices led us here, I'd be hard pressed to find a greater culprit than former Attorney General Merrick Garland. Given everything that has happened since Donald Trump returned to power last January, you could hardly be blamed if you were unaware that Garland--who Barack Obama unsuccessfully nominated to replace Antonin Scalia on the Supreme Court and who served as Joe Biden's attorney general--got a new job. It's an old job, really: He returned to the corporate law firm Arnold & Porter, where he had previously been a partner, to work on including white collar defense. Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. ? White collar defense, which often involves helping the rich and powerful escape accountability, is also the best way to describe Garland's tenure as attorney general, at least where it matters. While Garland's DOJ immediately began to prosecute the lowest-level participants in Trump's crimes against democracy--the foot soldiers of Jan. 6--Garland steadfastly refused to take on the architect of that insurrection, to bring federal charges against Trump himself. Indeed, Garland only took action after Congress's Jan. 6 committee him to launch the prosecutorial effort he'd spent years resisting. By that time, it was--in the most predictable way imaginable--already too late. Trump was running for reelection, meaning he could cast his prosecution as political persecution. He would be reelected before the cases against him had any chance to be concluded. Where accountability mattered, Garland failed spectacularly. This, and the resulting dystopian reality we are living through today, were not necessary or foregone conclusions. Another path was eminently possible, as a veritable pileup of international counterexamples demonstrates. Just this February, South Korea's former president Yoon Suk Yeol was for his imposition of martial law in December 2024. Last November, a Peruvian court an 11-year sentence to former president Pedro Castillo for his attempt to dissolve Peru's Congress in December 2022. And last September, Brazil's highest court former president Jair Bolsonaro to 27 years in prison for his efforts to overturn that country's 2022 election results. | | ---|---|--- The Brazilian comparison is particularly instructive, because of the beat-for-beat similarities between Bolsonaro and Trump. Both are right-wing populists who falsely insisted they had won an election they had lost. Both used tactics of denial and conspiracy to inspire violent attacks against their respective capitols with the goal of blocking a democratic transition of power. But the paths of these authoritarian despots diverged sharply following their attempted coups. One is currently in prison. The other is back in control of the most powerful nation on Earth, waging an all-out assault on our Constitution that frankly makes the crimes of his first term look like child's play. Given this tragic sequence of events, it is not, I think, too soon for those of us opposed to Trump's corrupt and cruel reign of terror--and in particular for our ostensible opposition party, whose leaders failed so utterly in their previous attempt to bring Trump to justice--to begin thinking seriously about what accountability for the crimes of this regime will look like if (and needless to say, it is a big if) Democrats are able to take back Congress and the presidency. Clearly, the Garland approach failed. What should replace it? | | ---|---|--- The only appropriate answer is the zealous pursuit of justice at every level of this criminal enterprise of an administration. The next Democratic administration should extend the Garland approach to January 6--a focus on the criminal foot soldiers of the Trump regime--to a host of other areas, most notably immigration enforcement, foreign policy, and corruption. But it shouldn't stop there, as the response to January 6 did. It must go further. Justice not only for the ICE and CBP thugs who murdered Americans in the streets, but also for the senior advisors and cabinet secretaries who sent those thugs on their campaigns of stochastic terrorism. Justice for the goons who will, it seems , seek to rig our upcoming elections, and the higher-level apparatchiks devising those antidemocratic schemes. Justice not just for the officials who executed double-tap strikes against civilians and bombed elementary schools and committed other startlingly , but more importantly, for the leaders who criminally launched such brazenly illegal military actions and wars. And, of course, justice for everyone inside and outside of this administration engaging in the most incomprehensibly of America's public resources in our history. Admittedly, all of this is a tall order. Pursuing accountability with such breadth and depth would require a serious commitment of resources, attention, and political capital. But it's a necessary, not an optional, step towards rebuilding our democracy, which--even in this ideal future in which Democrats have overcome Trump's efforts to dismantle free elections to win back temporary control of the government--will be overwhelmingly fragile for a long time to come. As the Allies understood when devising their for Germany after World War II, America simply cannot afford to allow the bandits, propagandists, and sadists who've been running this administration to simply slide back into positions of power and privilege from which to plot their next fascist takeover. If Garland's ignominious tenure as attorney general achieved nothing else of value, let it at least have taught us this lesson. Of course, these prosecutions would be polarizing; in today's political environment, there's little that is not, though much of this administration's conduct that merits prosecution enjoys supermajority levels of reprobation from the public. But a push for accountability, to succeed, will require a demonstration of popular support--in other words, a mandate. And that means it is incumbent on Democrats to make this fight for accountability a key part of their platform, starting now. This will make many Democratic leaders squeamish. The party's centrist establishment hates to take strong stances on just about anything. And there may be opposition from some on the left, as well. After all, doesn't this "prosecute Trump" fixation risk dragging us back to a pre-2020 resistance liberalism that deprioritized material conditions and obscured the structural problems of oligarchy, of which Trump is really just a symptom? Well, it could, if done poorly. But it could also buttress a much more powerful populist message, of the kind that Democrats desperately need to embrace if they are going to beat the diminished but still-potent right-wing populism of Trump and his MAGA heirs. | | ---|---|--- The word "populism" is thrown around a lot to describe very different political tendencies, in large part because populist anger can be channeled in polar opposite directions, towards fascism on the one hand or social democracy on the other. But at its core, populism is what you get when a critical mass of a society stops seeing the previous systems of political authority as legitimate. And there is nothing--literally nothing--that creates that perception of illegitimacy more than repeated demonstrations of elite impunity. This dynamic is the foundation of our current political crisis. Indeed, elite impunity is what created Donald Trump, whose pledges to tear the system down triumphed twice against candidates who responded to his anti-system rhetoric by defending that system. In 2016 and 2024 Trump cast himself as an outsider who was being attacked precisely because he represented a threat to America's political establishment and economic and cultural elite. For many, the alarm with which Trump was greeted only solidified this status. Finally, someone was promising to deliver some much-needed punishment to those who deserved it. In a world where regular people have watched again and again as rich assholes hollowed out their communities and denuded their lives and faced zero consequences for their crimes, Trump's --"For those who've been wronged and betrayed, I am your retribution"--starts to sound pretty good. At least someone's talking about retribution. Obviously, that was never the reality of Trumpism, and today Trump's administration stands as the ultimate monument to elite impunity. There are countless examples of how his regime has become a platonic ideal of the corrupt swamp, from the operation it has been running for wealthy criminals of all stripes, to the DOJ's announcement that it simply won't be anymore. But the clearest narrative connecting Trump and elite impunity--indeed, the most intuitively understandable indictment of how our institutions have failed to hold elites accountable for their depravity--is the one that's for months been flowing out of the millions of documents that make up the Epstein files. It's worth noting here that our old friend Merrick Garland sat on the Epstein files for four years without raising a finger to seek justice for Epstein's victims or raise awareness about his accomplices, enablers, and associates--the latter group of which includes Epstein's longtime friend Donald Trump, who sent him a card referencing a "wonderful secret" that would "never age," and who has been accused of trafficking and sexually assaulting a 13-year-old girl whom the FBI later found credible enough to four times. Thanks to horrifying references like these, the Trump administration has become deeply entangled and, in the eyes of many voters, incriminated in the Epstein saga. And that means Democrats have an opportunity to develop a broader message of opposition to elite impunity--one that rightfully combines pledges to hold both Epstein's associates and the Trump administration accountable for their wanton criminality. Because the truth is, these two groups are one and the same. As Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff , "We were told that MAGA was for working-class Americans. But this is a government of, by, and for the ultra-rich. It's the wealthiest cabinet ever. This is the Epstein class. They are the elites they pretend to hate." It's a message Democrats can run--and govern--on. Remember the system you so despised, with its one set of rules for you and me and another for the wealthy and powerful? The system that let Jeffrey Epstein off with a slap on the wrist because he was rich and well-connected? The system that transferred teen sex trafficker Ghislaine Maxwell to a cushy minimum security prison where she is waited on hand and foot by prison officials and was given a puppy? Well, that's the same system that's been working to protect Epstein's longtime friend Donald Trump and all his sycophantic deputies--like Trump's Commerce Secretary, Howard Lutnick, a documented visitor to Epstein's pedophile island--from being held accountable for their many crimes. And this time it's the Democrats who are promising to burn that god-forsaken system of elite impunity down to the ground. Of course, it would be madness at this point to trust the Democratic establishment--so long led by the likes of , , and , each of whom spent years consorting with Epstein--to embrace this message. Thankfully, 2028 offers Democrats an opportunity to wipe the slate clean of their decrepitly complicit establishment. This is one of the Democrats' greatest advantages right now. As Marjorie Taylor Greene's from GOP politics has demonstrated, taking on Epstein means taking on Trump, and no politician can become the next Republican presidential nominee by running against Trump. But our next Democratic nominee absolutely can--and must--commit to waging a war on the Epstein class, prosecuting its horrors, and rooting out the larger culture of elite impunity that is destroying our country from within. That promise not only gives Democrats a powerful populist message to run on--it also sets them up to demonstrate a real popular mandate, post-election, to bring the perpetrators of this regime's horrific crimes to justice. This January, Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva held a rally in front of a massive banner reading "Defense of Democracy." He was there to veto legislation that Brazil's opposition-controlled Congress had passed to lower Bolsonaro's sentence from 27 to two years. After describing Bolsonaro's attempted coup as a reminder that "democracy is not an unshakeable achievement," , "In the name of the future, we do not have the right to forget the past." Unlike Lula, America's last Democratic administration failed to appreciate this essential truth. It is quite possible that this failure will prove lethal to our democracy. But if it's not--if we are so fortunate as to have an opportunity to drive MAGA from power in 2026 and 2028--Democrats cannot be allowed to repeat their past mistakes. We must bring the architects of our current nightmare to justice--not in the name of the past, but in the name of the future. | | ---|---|--- This essay appeared in , a great outlet you can also follow on . We've got a few episodes already recorded that I'm actually really proud of. | Good afternoon Friend,
Few events in modern history changed the world as dramatically as COVID-19. But one of the biggest questions still lingers: **how did it start?** Internationally recognized author **Matt Ridley** helped investigate that question in his bestselling book **Viral: The Search for the Origin of COVID-19** , which examined the competing explanations for the pandemic and brought global attention to the possibility of a laboratory accident in Wuhan. Now, Ridley — the **5th Viscount Ridley and a member of the British House of Lords** — is coming to Jackson.

| [ ](https://mspolicy.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=60d4052c66b6745831ccdf7c8&id=6dca38a441&e=5703353baa)

While Ridley became widely known for his work on the origins of COVID-19, he is also one of the world’s leading voices on energy, innovation, and economic growth — and a close friend of U.S. Energy Secretary **Chris Wright**. Seats for this exclusive lunch are limited. If you would like to hear from one of the most influential thinkers examining some of the biggest global questions of our time, we hope you will join us.

Trump's heir, or Trump himself, with a court ready to block votes, redraw maps, and bury challenges. The door closes. Maybe for good.
The butterfly effect.

name: Ruben Gallego
subject: Fulton County came first. Now they want Maricopa’s voter rolls.
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Bondi subpoenaed the voter rolls for Maricopa County the other day — the largest county in my state with nearly 4.8 million people.
#

Peter, it's Ruben.
I’m going to say this at the top: This isn’t a fundraising email. I just want to tell you about something that’s been happening over the last few months. There’s too much going on for any one person to track, but this is important.
In January, Trump and Pam Bondi raided the Fulton County, Georgia elections office. Additionally, Bondi made turning over the Minnesota voter rolls one of the preconditions for a drawdown in Minneapolis. That’s the election processes of two swing states that Trump is trying to pressure and manipulate.
Now, he’s coming after Arizona. Bondi subpoenaed the voter rolls for Maricopa County the other day — the largest county in my state with nearly 4.8 million people. Trump never got over losing in Arizona in 2020, and he’s going to lie, cheat, and steal as much as he has to so he can hold on to power this year.
Let’s get into this: There were 3 allegations of voter fraud that ended in a criminal conviction in the 2020 cycle in Arizona. 3.4 MILLION Arizonans voted. Think about that. Let’s put it a little differently: A LOT more people every year get struck by lightning than are charged with voter fraud. Like, it’s not even close.
This isn’t about voter fraud. It wasn’t in 2020, it wasn’t when I beat Kari Lake in 2024, and that’s not what it’s about now. This is about making people feel like their votes won’t count. Trump wants people to believe that the system can’t change, that it’s corrupt, that only he can fix it.
So, I want you to hear this from me: Trump is going to try to steal the election this November. Same as he always does. And I am going to do everything I can to make sure that does not happen.
But more than that: There are literally millions of good, honest people — both Republicans and Democrats, elected officials, election workers, and volunteers that care about our democracy — standing in Trump’s way. We need to have their backs.
We’ve got to take this threat seriously. But do not, for one second, think that Trump’s already won — he hasn’t. The only way he does is if we cut and run, and that is not going to happen.
Hang tough, we’re in this together.
Semper Fi,
Ruben

name: Jackson Lahmeyer
subject: To DC... Pray For Me
body:
Today, Oklahoma Congressman Kevin Hern announced that he will no longer seek re-election for Congressional District 1 but instead pursue the open US S
| | |
---
Today, **Oklahoma Congressman Kevin Hern** announced that he will no longer seek re-election for Congressional District 1 but instead pursue the open US Senate seat in Oklahoma. When I was asked if I would seek the open Senate seat, I ruled it out immediately because I know what it takes to run a state-wide race and would not have been a wise move for me or my family. However, now that my congressional District is open (CD1). I am considering running for this open seat which covers just the Tulsa Metro. I am headed to DC for a round of meetings tomorrow at the White House about this decision. Please pray for me that I will have wisdom and clarity on which path to go. To my [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14407.1.0b72ec2ff0ba3142f7b911f78cf5b2ac) family, whether I run or do not run. Just know that for the main thing will always be the main thing and I will continue being the Pastor of [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14408.1.8c71ec0bf8814aaaab15d3620e1e3b16). Also, be sure to check out some upcoming events at [Sheridan.Church](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14409.1.fc78a6cc67552a3849bb9c0f228f3f91) **Upcoming Events At Sheridan** : -Sun, Mar 15 @6:30pm: Tough Q's About Israel w/**Reverend Johnnie Moore** & **Tulsa Jewish Federation**. RSVP for FREE here: [https://jewishtulsa.org/event/moore/](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14410.1.d650e4b01b4cf80b5635e87faf9777b5) -Wed, April 8 @6:30pm: **Rabbi Jonathan Cahn** -Thur, April 9: **Tim Tebow** -Sun, May 24 @10am: **Pastor Andrew Sedra** -June 19-20: **Remnant Rising w/Eric Trump, General Flynn & many others**... -Oct 8-9: **Flashpoint w/Gene Bailey + others** Please consider giving to the mission of [Sheridan](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14411.1.40f741686ee5b3b37e49b9014a7a1b86): [https://sheridan.church/give/](https://email.cloud2.secureclick.net/c/5961?id=27911766.14412.1.cd418a8e19cdce1e64ff42cca999f7d5) Thank you, Pastor Jackson Lahmeyer

body:

# We Need Your Help to Win This!
---
|
---
| |
With the election less than 60 days away, I thought I would take a little time again to write to all of you so that we can work together to win this in May! To win this we need your help by getting my name out there, helping at the polls, introducing your friends, co-workers, and family to the movement we are building and reaching out on our website! Our website ([haggardforcongress.com](https://hoosiersforhaggard.us12.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b9e7cbafb97c2110b065cece3&id=88ce1c7b36&e=72dace1453)) has a great feature where you can reach out and show your support. At the bottom of our front page, scroll down and find the **Get Involved** section. There you will see this:

---
|
---
| | Whether it is introducing someone or a group of people to our team, **grabbing a yard sign** , a small donation, or helping on election day, please reach out on our website and we will get in contact with you shortly! It takes a team to win this and we want to build a coalition that will work to represent you! We look forward to seeing your name showing support soon!
---
|
---
| | I will continue highlighting the endorsements I continue to receive throughout the district from local leaders and groups that put their faith in me to represent them in Congress. Our momentum is just getting started and I can’t wait to continue to share with you who is already on board. If you ever want to get involved or endorse, please reach out!

| Peter,

I want to talk about something that’s been at the core of my work long before this campaign: **defending our democracy.**

In 2020, Michigan was at the center of national attention. After the presidential election, Donald Trump and his cronies tried everything to discredit our results and overturn the will of Michigan voters. They pushed baseless claims about vote counting in Detroit, tried to block certification of the results, and spread lies designed to weaken public confidence in our democracy.

**But Michigan fought back. We stood strong. And we proved that our elections are fair and our votes count.

As Chair of the Michigan Senate Elections Committee, I am proud to still be on the frontlines of that fight.**

Now, I’m running for Congress because Michigan deserves leaders who stand up for the values of democracy and fight back against anyone trying to tear it down. I need your help to keep pushing for transparency, integrity, and accountability at every level of government.

clean_body: I want to talk about something that’s been at the core of my work long before this campaign: defending our democracy. | = | Peter, I want to talk about something that’s been at the core of my work long before this campaign: defending our democracy. In 2020, Michigan was at the center of national attention. After the presidential election, Donald Trump and his cronies tried everything to discredit our results and overturn the will of Michigan voters. They pushed baseless claims about vote counting in Detroit, tried to block certification of the results, and spread lies designed to weaken public confidence in our democracy. But Michigan fought back. We stood strong. And we proved that our elections are fair and our votes count. As Chair of the Michigan Senate Elections Committee, I am proud to still be on the frontlines of that fight. Now, I’m running for Congress because Michigan deserves leaders who stand up for the values of democracy and fight back against anyone trying to tear it down. I need your help to keep pushing for transparency, integrity, and accountability at every level of government. = | | | = | = | = | = | = Thank you for caring about democracy as much as I do. In our last email, we looked at the disregard for human rights. Today, we examine the third sign of fascism: **The Identification of Enemies as a Unifying Cause.** Fascist movements thrive by redirecting public frustration away from systemic failures and toward "the other." By branding specific groups as existential threats, they create a unifying frenzy used to justify the suspension of civil liberties. We see this playbook in action today.
