It doesn’t stop there: Trump is doubling down, saying he won’t sign _any_ legislation unless this voter suppression bill reaches his desk.
This bill is nothing but red tape and costs for voters -- and it’ll fall hardest on communities that have already had to fight for equal access: seniors, married women who’ve changed their names, voters of color, and young people.
If we don’t push back now, the tools that make registration possible like online systems, mail, and community drives could be gutted.
**[Free and fair elections are sacred – I'll always fight to protect our democracy. Will you stand with me in defense of every American at the ballot box?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127142895/607072102/-464955694?refcode=em-3.11.26-all-b&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3ODciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiODgyMDdkYWYtOTUxZC1mMTExLTlhNDgtMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=c1ytuwy_pCHfmLnKjqqFNbhyU8ZTgIBUSiHFsNQSLdE=&emci=80207daf-951d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=88207daf-951d-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=27336212)**

Angie Nixon is leading policies for affordable housing, equitable healthcare, universal early childcare, strong public schools, fair wages, reproductive justice, and more.
Her leadership is rooted in community and lived experience―watching her mom work two jobs to get by, attending public schools and getting bused across town because her predominantly Black neighborhood school didn’t have adequate resources, and losing her cousin to gun violence.
She’s running for U.S. Senate because too many families are working harder than ever and still falling behind, while billionaires buy our democracy and rig the economy in their favor.****
**Angie believes that our future should be shaped by teachers, nurses, parents, and workers―not special interests.**
She has built a reputation in Florida’s capital as an outspoken fighter who is unafraid to confront corruption and powerful interests. We need her in Congress.

She has served as a union organizer and the head of a statewide coalition that registered tens of thousands of new voters. Now, Angie is running for U.S. Senate to build a people-powered government that puts families first―not billionaire bullies and greedy corporations. | Angie Nixon is leading policies for affordable housing, equitable healthcare, universal early childcare, strong public schools, fair wages, reproductive justice, and more. name: Deb Haaland
subject: Meet Zia! 🐾
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
I'm so excited to introduce you to the newest member of my family and of the Team Haaland pack

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)
---
Hi, friend, it's Deb, and I'm so excited to introduce you to the newest member of my family and of the Team Haaland pack: **Zia**!
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5902?refcode=jtk258-fr-nd&t=2&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)
I rescued her and named her after the iconic Zia sun — an emblem New Mexicans are proud of and one you can find everywhere in our state, from our state flag and license plates to my very own campaign logo.
The Zia sun is a sacred symbol to the Indigenous people of Zia Pueblo. It holds deep beauty and significance for our state, our people, and for me. It also reflects something special about New Mexico — the way we look out for one another and care for our communities.

As someone who comes from 35 generations of Laguna Pueblo women, that spirit guides how I live, how I lead, and how I’m running this campaign — because I want to make sure every New Mexican has the chance to thrive.
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5902?refcode=jtk258-fr-nd&t=3&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)
---
I have never forgotten my roots, friend, and I never will.

I was once a single mom living paycheck to paycheck, relying on programs like SNAP, WIC, and Medicaid to help keep my child fed and healthy. That’s when I knew I wanted to make sure government and our leaders worked for the people — not the other way around.

So I became an organizer, then Chair of the Democratic Party of New Mexico, one of the first Native women elected to Congress, and later the first Native Cabinet Secretary.

Every step of the way, I’ve stayed true to who I’ve always been: a fighter and a protector for New Mexicans.

And that will never change.
I am ready to fight for higher wages, lower costs, safer neighborhoods, and strong education for your children. I am ready to push back when Trump wants to drag his dangerous, extremists ideas to New Mexico. I am ready to be the governor New Mexico needs.

But I can’t do it alone. That’s why I have an incredible campaign team, it’s why I have Zia and friend, it’s why I am reaching out to you. I don't have the means to self-fund my campaign like many of my opponents do, but I do have tens of thousands of folks like you who believe that New Mexico needs a governor who will fight fiercely for our home and our people.
_[Our average online donation this month is just $21.31.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6166?refcode=jtk258-fr-nd&t=4&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)_ That means this campaign is powered by a steady stream of people-powered support that allows us to build momentum across our beautiful state and win.
**So on this special day, as we welcome Zia to our family and this grassroots team, I am humbly asking:_[Will you please chip in $21.31 or anything you can today to support our campaign?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6166?refcode=jtk258-fr-nd&t=5&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)_**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5902?refcode=jtk258-fr-nd&t=6&akid=8128%2E400544%2EGfdQ-l)
---
Be Fierce,

Deb
|

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

Through her work in behavioral health, she’s helped people access mental health care, navigate crises, and find stability when systems meant to support them fall short. Those experiences shape how Sierra approaches leadership. She knows that when Harrisburg fails to invest in mental health care, community services, and the workers who provide that care, families feel the consequences every single day. And she hasn’t just witnessed these challenges — she’s been organizing to change them. As President of the National Association of Social Workers – Pennsylvania Chapter, Sierra has brought advocates from across the state to Harrisburg to push for stronger behavioral health systems, better crisis response, and real investment in the workforce that keeps our communities healthy. That’s exactly the kind of leadership the Working Families Party is proud to support. clean_body: | | | Peter, We’re excited about this one. Every so often, a candidate comes along who already embodies the kind of leadership we want to see more of in Harrisburg — someone who has spent years doing the work in their community and knows exactly what needs to change. That’s Sierra McNeil. Today, the Pennsylvania Working Families Party is proud to endorse Sierra McNeil for State Representative in the 195th District. Sierra is a social worker, educator, and Strawberry Mansion neighbor who has spent her career working directly with families across North Philadelphia. Through her work in behavioral health, she’s helped people access mental health care, navigate crises, and find stability when systems meant to support them fall short. Those experiences shape how Sierra approaches leadership. She knows that when Harrisburg fails to invest in mental health care, community services, and the workers who provide that care, families feel the consequences every single day. And she hasn’t just witnessed these challenges — she’s been organizing to change them. As President of the National Association of Social Workers – Pennsylvania Chapter, Sierra has brought advocates from across the state to Harrisburg to push for stronger behavioral health systems, better crisis response, and real investment in the workforce that keeps our communities healthy. That’s exactly the kind of leadership the Working Families Party is proud to support. Now we’re working to help power Sierra’s campaign and make sure voters across the district hear about the vision she’s bringing to this race. Peter,

While the rise in popularity of politicians like Zohran Mamdani and his socialist policies might have come as a shock to many, I've been warning people about it for years.

Younger Americans do not know what socialism means.

When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark.

They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist.

**Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand.**

Rand wrote novels like _We The Living_ , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, _Atlas Shrugged_ , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement."

The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do.

That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events.

I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas.

Otherwise, please let me explain why I believe The Atlas Society and its leadership are best suited to combat the rise in popularity of these harmful ideologies.

First, Jennifer and I go back more than 35 years, when she was a White House Speechwriter, and Americans for Tax Reform was in its founding era. She's one of the most innovative, effective, and persevering executives I know. Over the past decade, she's built The Atlas Society into a juggernaut for freedom.

**The Atlas Society is the ONLY non-profit adapting Rand 's works into media that appeals to young Americans. **

Just one example: their animated book trailer for _Atlas Shrugged_ drew 12 million views, and DOUBLED sales of the novel! They're currently producing a full-length feature film of Anthem, Rand's dystopian novella.

I believe in their great work because I've seen the impact they've had.

It's why I've collaborated with The Atlas Society on various discussions and interviews, including speaking at their student conferences, doing interviews on their podcast, and even doing stand-up comedy at one of their fundraising galas!

clean_body: Peter, While the rise in popularity of politicians like Zohran Mamdani and his socialist policies might have come as a shock to many, I've been warning people about it for years. Younger Americans do not know what socialism means. When younger Americans think of "socialism," they think it means Sweden and Denmark. They didn't grow up during the Cold War. They don't remember the Soviet Union. Or Stalin's Gulags or the Warsaw Pact. They couldn't even tell you what the initials U.S.S.R. stood for, or that Nazi is the abbreviation of National Socialist. Young Americans need to hear about socialism, real socialism, from someone who experienced it firsthand. I can think of no one better than Ayn Rand. Rand wrote novels like We The Living , which dramatized the inhumanity of the Soviet system -- and most importantly, Atlas Shrugged , which dramatized what would happen if socialism came to America. Rand's immense success in making the moral case for capitalism led my friend, the late Ed Crane, to call her "the greatest all-time recruiter for the liberty movement." The challenge is that young people simply aren't reading novels anymore. In the 70s, 70% of young people read fiction daily for fun -- today, less than 12% do. That's where The Atlas Society comes in. They bring Ayn Rand's ideas to life for new audiences in innovative ways, including animated videos, viral social media, graphic novels -- even music videos. Plus online courses and live events. I told Jennifer Grossman, The Atlas Society's CEO, that I would help her raise $30,000 online this month to introduce more young minds to Ayn Rand's ideas. Otherwise, please let me explain why I believe The Atlas Society and its leadership are best suited to combat the rise in popularity of these harmful ideologies. # [The city that built America](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=190033295&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkwMDMzMjk1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzMyNzAxMzgsImV4cCI6MTc3NTg2MjEzOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.sC4hjy1Zt2mZJTHn38DcPx1wS0SAPwn-zJFr6OvpJ2A)
### Why I'm fighting for places like Ecorse, Michigan.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 11
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..C7Ig-VceEaQ4WrlESn2QbBG1jV6_7Bfg8IOjnSWKWh0?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/the-city-that-built-america?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Last month, I got to spend some time with Mayor Lamar Tidwell in Ecorse - one of the oldest cities in Wayne County.
If you've never been to Ecorse, here's something you should know: **This is the city that built America:**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ce4a32f9-3a19-4b7f-b5d5-c4d0763619c4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Ecorse sits along the Detroit River, surrounded by the factories and plants that powered Michigan's industrial rise. Generations of workers in this community welded frames, loaded ships, and did the hard work that made this country run.
**You can feel that history when you 're there. It's a snapshot of Michigan's legacy - full of hardworking people right on the Detroit River.**
But like so many manufacturing communities across our state, Ecorse has had its share of tough moments, too. In 2020, when U.S. Steel shuttered its factory, **more than a thousand workers lost their jobs overnight.**
That's not just a statistic. Those are real families. Real paychecks gone. Pride in building something for our country. The ripple effects of that loss were felt across the entire community.
But what I've always admired about Ecorse is they're not spending their time dwelling on the loss.
**They 're determined to reinvent. Reinvest. Rebuild.**
Mayor Tidwell talked to me about what reinvestment really means for a place like Ecorse. Not just patching things up, but rebuilding in a way that honors the workers who have been the heart of the city for more than a century.
Because that kind of redevelopment is what this country is about. It's what Michigan is about.
Michiganders don't fold when times get tough. We roll up our sleeves and get to work.
That's why I've been fighting to bring more federal dollars to partner with Ecorse as they redevelop and rebuild.
**Places like Ecorse shouldn 't be overlooked, not after everything they've given to this country.**
When I was driving through the city with Mayor Tidwell, we talked about what federal leadership should give to communities like this. About how the workers who powered America's manufacturing economy deserve investment and opportunity as they move into their next chapter.
That can mean supporting their medical clinic, funding the library, or investing in the port. At the heart of it, it's about making sure federal dollars help communities like Ecorse move forward.
**Because while Ecorse has faced hard times, today the city is on the verge of something exciting - and I'm proud to stand with them in that fight.**
Places like Ecorse are why I love Michigan. They have an incredible history. But more importantly, in the **city that built America** , the people of Ecorse are showing the nation what Michigan grit looks like once again.
If you want to hear more about what's happening in Ecorse - and the fight to support Michigan's manufacturing communities - I hope you'll take a few minutes to watch my conversation with Mayor Tidwell.
We drove through the city together and talked about its history, its present, and the fight for what's ahead.
With grit,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

name: America Fitzpatrick, LCV
subject: TAKE ACTION: Say NO to Arctic Refuge drilling
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM1NDY5OTYS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQyMTAyMTA0OQS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
The Arctic Refuge is Not for Sale!

The Trump administration has opened the lease sale for oil and gas drilling in
the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. It’s time to speak out: The Arctic Refuge is not for sale.

The Arctic Refuge is irreplaceable. It should be protected, not leased for oil and gas drilling. Decades of Indigenous leadership and
sustained pressure from people like you have kept oil companies out of the
Arctic Refuge, and it’s crucial that they stay out.

Let’s keep the pressure up. Tell Secretary Burgum: No oil and gas drilling in the Arctic Refuge. Not now, not ever. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/vNR6fE7-3-c_ ADD YOUR NAME >> https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/dmyWFL4pYpC- Peter, There has never been drilling in the Arctic Refuge, and it’s up to all of us to
keep it that way. For decades, the Gwich'in people have led the movement to keep
the Arctic Refuge free from corporate greed and extraction — no drilling, no
development. LCV stands with the Gwich’in people and opposes lease sales on their sacred
lands, and in the entire region. Will you stand with us? Add your voice today and help protect the Arctic Refuge for generations to come. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/9zEZMdN-z-M- The Arctic Refuge is irreplaceable. It should be protected, not exploited. Congressional Republicans enacted a law that mandates lease
sales for the Refuge, but nothing requires oil companies to participate — and so
far, the environmental movement has been able to hold the line to keep Big Oil
out. We must continue to speak out so Big Oil and lawmakers hear loud and clear:
we oppose drilling in the Arctic Refuge, because nothing justifies selling off one of the last wild places on Earth. Thanks to public pressure, even Trump’s Big Oil cronies won’t touch the Arctic.
Major oil companies recognize that drilling in the Refuge is financially risky,
publicly unpopular, and incompatible with a rapidly changing Arctic. In 2019, BP
pulled out of the Arctic and Alaska completely, signaling the clear risks for drilling. On top of that, not a single bidder
showed up in the most recent lease sale in 2025. Let’s keep it that way. If Arctic Refuge drilling ever were to occur, it would have disastrous
consequences for Indigenous communities and the Gwich'in people, as well as for
our climate. These lands are irreplaceable, and no amount of corporate
interference for profit should ever be acceptable. The Arctic Refuge has endured decades of political attacks. It has survived
because Indigenous-led movements and people like you refuse to let oil companies
turn this region — essential for our shared human, animal, and environmental
well-being — into another oil and gas graveyard. We must continue to oppose drilling in the Refuge and send a clear message to
oil companies: The Arctic Refuge is not for sale. Take action today >> https://links.messages.lcv. Thank you for standing with LCV and with all the protectors of the Arctic Refuge
— so that this irreplaceable wilderness may continue to thrive for future
generations. America Fitzpatrick
Conservation Program Director

It’s time to stop playing it safe and start delivering real solutions for working people.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260311-1&t=1&akid=3236%2E587540%2EOdwA52)
Peter,
We asked. And more than 3,000 of you answered.
No, seriously! Last month, we sent out a survey asking an important question: _If Democrats win back power, what should we actually do with it?_
Thousands of you told us exactly what you want to see from the Democratic Party, and the message was loud and clear: **stop playing it safe and start delivering for working people.**
First, I want to say thank you for taking the time to give us your input. This is how we build a party that wins — by listening to the people we’re fighting for.
**[This will be a lengthy email, so before I get into it, can you pitch in $5 to support our work? If we’re serious about building the power we need to implement our progressive policy agenda, we have to start strong and start early. That means investing in progressive fighters right now who will champion our issues in Congress.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260311_1_project.X1ktNb&refcode=em20260311-3236&amount=5&t=2&akid=3236%2E587540%2EOdwA52)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260311_1_project.X1ktNb&amount=5&refcode=em20260311-3236&t=3&akid=3236%2E587540%2EOdwA52)**
Here’s what rose to the top:
**78% of respondents chose issues related to _the affordability crisis._**
Honestly, this was the loudest message we heard. People are working harder than ever to stay alive, but costs are crushing working people. Housing, health care, and childcare costs need to come down while wages go up, so working families can actually afford to buy a home and build a stable life.
**72% of respondents chose issues related to _our fundamental rights._**
Basic rights shouldn’t depend on which state someone lives in. That means codifying abortion rights, protecting LGBTQ+ communities, ending ICE’s reign of terror, and guaranteeing humane immigration policies that create a real pathway to citizenship while treating people with dignity and care.
**67% of respondents chose issues related to _corruption and corporate power._**

Adelita for Congress Newsletter

Join **Congresswoman Grijalva** this **Saturday, March 14th** , to knock doors, talk to voters, and collect even more signatures to send a **FIGHTER** back to Congress!
